question.note: Whether substance use is associated with nominations (sender, receiver, homophily) in AI-majority schools 'as it often does in racially heterogeneous schools': Q2 and Q3; also the substance use part of Q1.
Reciprocity, friends of friends, and degree concentration.
Demographic part of Q1 (gender, grade, sexual orientation).

central_claim.note: 'Existing friendships' stands for the structural mechanisms (reciprocity, transitivity) the quote does not name, a loose wording; with shared demographics against substance use it states C1. The depression and AI identity clause is the abstract's (F4 content, not credited here).

flags.text: The note says reservation schools 'should not be treated as interchangeable' in prevention design; the paper says interventions 'may need to be calibrated to school-specific relational ecologies rather than applied uniformly across reservation settings' (p.16).

central_claim.note: Accurate to p.16 apart from the hedge; school-specific calibration is not C3, which is about the assumption that friendship rests on substance use.

evidence.note: Three schools on one Northern Plains reservation, grades 9 and 10 (E1, as in the qwen-slots calibration; 'cross-sectional' is in the next entry); 263 respondents and 247 with complete network data, stages named correctly (E2; 77% not given, treated as detail); school types (E7).
Directed nominations, up to ten friends from a roster; adds 'cross-sectional survey'.
Advisory board review of measures (p.6): accurate, not in the gold.
Substance use as binary ever-use; ceremonial tobacco excluded (p.7).
Six CES-D questions and six adapted MEIM affirmation and belonging items.

Demographic terms as description and adjustment, straight versus non-straight (p.6, p.8): accurate. This is the first sentence of L6 without its causal caveat (which the note gives in scope_and_limits), so not credited as misplaced.
Per-school base ERGM and substance models with sender/receiver/similarity terms and the two-path term; AMEs in the next entry.
Peer-perception imputation and the sensitivity analysis; the change in some significance levels is accurate (p.7).
Goodness-of-fit check against 100 simulated networks (p.12): accurate, not in the gold.

key_findings.note: Reciprocity given through the descriptive rates (the norm in all three schools) and transitivity net of two-paths.
Both exceptions located; marijuana homophily correctly called marginal.

scope_and_limits.note: Two grades at one time point; developmental change and school transitions.
The paper offers kinship networks as a possible arena for identity effects and calls for research in heterogeneous schools (p.15); the note keeps the hedge. Not a gold answer.

Future-research points from p.17 (community contexts, governance, qualitative work on using friendships in interventions). Does not claim the authors said three schools cannot disentangle school features (L-x1).

theoretical_positioning.note: Network analysis kept, with mechanism strength treated as culturally and institutionally contingent; as the haiku calibration entry (T2, T1 partial). 'Extend' is not flagged.

flags.text: The note says the authors 'revise rather than reject network-based prevention'; the paper says the findings 'challenge assumptions underpinning many network-based prevention programs' and that endogenous factors suggest 'a promising direction' (p.1, p.14).

theoretical_positioning.note: Same call as the haiku 'revise the assumptions of network-based prevention work' entry: the challenge to prevention assumptions and the call for strengths-based alternatives is C3.
